lesson.title: The Return Pushes Back.
lesson.hook: Two connected decisions. Prepare, read the ball, choose.
lesson.liveIntro: Your wide serve is travelling. The returner can still change the next ball.

sr1A.name: Does this return still invite the angle?
sr1A.sit: The return drives you behind the baseline. You are still adjusting.
sr1A.q: Does this return still invite the angle?
opts: Force a sharp angle from behind the baseline
Give yourself height and depth through the middle

lines.A: The sharp angle goes wide in this example. The return removed the opening.
lines.B: Depth and height give margin from this deeper contact. Keep recovering.

sr1A.take: Being ready helps you adapt. It does not make every return attackable.
sr1A.payoff: Being ready helps you adapt. It does not make every return attackable.
sr1A.principle: Read the return you get. Change the plan when it changes.
sr1A.why: This return is deeper than the short-return point and moves your contact behind the baseline. Being ready helps you respond; it does not make a low-margin angle the right choice. Height and depth through the middle offer space and time to recover.

sr1B.name: Does this return still invite the angle?
sr1B.sit: You recover early, but their deeper return still pushes you back.
sr1B.q: Does this return still invite the angle?
opts: Force a sharp angle from behind the baseline
Give yourself height and depth through the middle

lines.A: Getting ready early did not make this angle easy. It goes wide here.
lines.B: You change the plan to fit the deeper return. The point continues.

sr1B.take: Being ready helps you adapt. It does not make every return attackable.
sr1B.payoff: Being ready helps you adapt. It does not make every return attackable.
sr1B.principle: Read the return you get. Change the plan when it changes.
sr1B.why: This return is deeper than the short-return point and moves your contact behind the baseline. Being ready helps you respond; it does not make a low-margin angle the right choice. Height and depth through the middle offer space and time to recover.

sr1.name: What do you do after serving?
sr1.sit: Your wide serve is travelling. The returner can still change the next ball.
sr1.q: What do you do after serving?
opts: Lean into the forehand plan before the return
Recover balanced, then respond to their hit

lines.A: You guess before seeing the return. Watch what comes back.
lines.B: You recover with options available, then read the return.

summaries.10: You recovered, but forced the angle from a deeper contact.
summaries.11: You recovered early and changed the plan for the deeper return.
summaries.01: You corrected your position and adapted to the deeper return.
summaries.00: The early guess cost preparation. The forced angle then went wide.

comparison.intro: Watch the same ball twice. Change only your preparation.

pro.label: Coach’s lens · Prepare, then decide
pro.moment: LTA coach Matt Smith describes closing distance with larger steps, making smaller adjustments near contact, and recovering after a shot.
pro.read: Our application: recover after the serve with room to respond. Read the actual return before deciding how much pressure it permits.
pro.src: LTA · Improve your tennis footwork · Matt Smith

drill.name: Prepare, then call it
drill.how: Have a partner alternate shorter and deeper returns. Recover after serving, then say “pressure” or “margin” from the return you see. Keep the rally going.
